{
  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "Inconsistent sample size between synopsis and statistical plan",
      "quote": "Approximately 76 patients will be enrolled.",
      "page": 15,
      "section": "Population",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The synopsis states approximately 76 patients will be enrolled, but the statistical plan says 72 patients are required with a 5% inflation for withdrawals, which yields 75.6, not 76. This discrepancy could cause confusion in sample size justification.",
      "fix": "Clarify the exact sample size (e.g., 76) and align the statistical plan text to state 'approximately 76' or adjust the inflation factor to yield 76."
    },
    {
      "title": "Primary endpoint hypothesis uses two-sided test but objective implies one-sided",
      "quote": "Ha: pCR rate ≠ 25%",
      "page": 16,
      "section": "Statistical Plan",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The null and alternative hypotheses are written as a two-sided test (≠), but the primary objective is to evaluate efficacy, which typically implies a one-sided test for superiority. The sample size calculation mentions 2-sided significance level, but the clinical question is whether pCR rate is greater than 25%. This inconsistency may lead to incorrect statistical inference.",
      "fix": "Specify a one-sided alternative (e.g., Ha: pCR rate > 25%) and adjust the sample size calculation accordingly, or justify the two-sided test."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing definition of 'selected patients with stage II CSCC'",
      "quote": "selected patients with stage II CSCC (≥3 cm longest diameter in an aesthetically sensitive region)",
      "page": 14,
      "section": "Study Design",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The protocol does not define what constitutes an 'aesthetically sensitive region' or how 'selected' is determined. This ambiguity could lead to inconsistent enrollment and difficulty in reproducing the study.",
      "fix": "Provide a clear definition of 'aesthetically sensitive region' (e.g., face, scalp, neck) and specify the selection criteria for stage II patients."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inconsistent timing of tumor response imaging",
      "quote": "will undergo tumor response imaging assessment prior to receiving the third dose of cemiplimab (day 43±3) and prior to surgery (day 85)",
      "page": 14,
      "section": "Study Part 1 (Neoadjuvant)",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The text says imaging is done prior to the third dose (day 43±3) and prior to surgery (day 85), but the surgery window is day 75-100. If surgery occurs earlier than day 85, the second imaging may not be feasible. The protocol does not specify how to handle imaging if surgery is earlier.",
      "fix": "Clarify that the second imaging should be performed within a window before surgery (e.g., within 14 days prior to surgery) and adjust the schedule accordingly."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing details on adjuvant radiation therapy",
      "quote": "At the investigator’s discretion, patients may alternatively receive adjuvant radiation therapy (concurrent or subsequent cemiplimab treatment not allowed) or enter an observation-only period.",
      "page": 14,
      "section": "Study Part 2 (Adjuvant)",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The protocol does not specify the dose, schedule, or duration of adjuvant radiation therapy, nor does it define how radiation therapy interacts with the study assessments and endpoints. This lack of detail could lead to variability in treatment and affect safety and efficacy analyses.",
      "fix": "Add a section describing the radiation therapy regimen (e.g., standard of care, dose, fractionation) and how it will be recorded and analyzed."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inconsistent definition of end of study",
      "quote": "The end of study is defined as the last visit of the last patient.",
      "page": 15,
      "section": "End of Study Definition",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The synopsis says end of study is the last visit of the last patient, but the follow-up section says patients are followed until disease recurrence or end of study, whichever occurs first. This could be interpreted as the end of study being the last visit of the last patient, but if a patient has recurrence, they may stop follow-up earlier, so the last visit may not be the last patient's final visit. Clarify the exact definition.",
      "fix": "Define end of study as the last visit of the last patient, and clarify that patients with recurrence may have their last visit earlier, but the study ends when the last patient has completed all required visits."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing details on independent central pathology review",
      "quote": "Following surgical tumor resection, the primary endpoint (pCR rate) will be assessed by an independent central pathology review committee.",
      "page": 14,
      "section": "Study Part 1 (Neoadjuvant)",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The protocol does not describe the composition, charter, or procedures of the independent central pathology review committee, nor how the pCR is defined (e.g., no viable tumor cells). This is critical for the primary endpoint and should be specified.",
      "fix": "Add a section detailing the central pathology review process, including the definition of pCR, handling of samples, and committee oversight."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing information on patient and public involvement",
      "quote": "Patients will be evaluated in clinic for up to 3 additional years.",
      "page": 15,
      "section": "Follow-Up",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The protocol does not mention any patient and public involvement in the design or conduct of the trial, which is a SPIRIT requirement. This is a gap in the protocol.",
      "fix": "Add a section describing patient and public involvement, or state that none was sought and why."
    }
  ]
}
